```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it
options(plotly.core.plotlyjs = "cdn")
version <- packageVersion('plotly.core')
```
<!-- #region -->
### Version Problems

In order to follow the examples in this documentation site, you should have the latest version of `plotly.core` installed (`r version`), as detailed in the [Getting Started](getting-started.html) guide. These pages are written for `plotly.core`, which is a different package from the legacy `plotly` R package: code written for `plotly` (`plot_ly()`, `layout()`, `subplot()`, ...) will not work here, and vice versa. `plotly.core` bundles its own copy of the Plotly.js rendering engine, so figures look the same wherever they are rendered. Read on for details about troubleshooting `plotly.core` in other environments.

### Import Problems

Most loading problems can be traced back to having multiple or outdated versions of `plotly.core` installed. It's often worthwhile to uninstall before following the [Getting Started](getting-started.html) instructions from scratch. You can run the following commands in the console to fully remove `plotly.core` before installing again:

```
remove.packages('plotly.core')
```

> Problems can also arise if you have a file named `plotly.core.R` in the same directory as the code you are executing.

### Static Image Export Problems

`plotly.core` does not use the `orca` executable. `save_image()` exports figures with headless Chrome (driven by the chromote package). If export fails because no browser is found, set the `CHROMOTE_CHROME` environment variable to the complete path of a Chrome or Chromium-based browser, or download Chrome Headless Shell once with `chromote::chrome_versions_add("latest-stable", "chrome-headless-shell")`. See [Static Image Export](static-image-export.html) for details.
